+
+Rules:
+
+- Criteria lines use the exact format `- ACn: <criterion>`.
+- Every criterion ends with [verify: exec `<command>`],
+  [verify: invariant `<command>`], [verify: judged] or
+  [verify: none — <reason>].
+- After `flow freeze` this file is checksum-protected: any edit outside
+  `keryx flow ac update` fails every gate and status transition.
+- Completion requires every ACn to be confirmed via
+  `keryx flow ac confirm <id> <ACn>`.
+
+Source of the wording: `docs/requirements/keryx-review-degradation/prd.md`, frozen by the operator on 2026-10-28 (Helyx message 230859). The reviewer is a generic keryx skill in the npm package, profile `full`; no project's own pipeline is wired in this flow.
+
+## Criteria
+
+- AC1: `review-degradation` exists as a skill under `.metaproject/skills/gdskills/review/review-degradation/SKILL.md` with a byte-identical bundled copy under `src/gdskills/bundled/skills/review/review-degradation/`, registered in `src/gdskills/catalog.ts` (tier `deep`, profile `full` only), `src/gdskills/skill-length-ceilings.ts` and `src/gdskills/bundled/install-manifest.json`; the existing catalog, ceiling and bundle-parity tests pass with the entry. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/`]
+- AC2: The skill states its one question, the seven classes (`behaviour-delta`, `default-change`, `diff-vs-description`, `debt`, `performance`, `cross-pr`, `blind-test`), the five evidence kinds (`probe`, `consumer-trace`, `merge-trace`, `red-test`, `base-diff`), the four output lanes and the shared laws, and says in its first screen how it differs from `review-regression`; it carries no project-specific rule name, path or quotation. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/review-degradation-skill.test.ts`]
+- AC3: `review-finding.schema.json` (every copy) accepts optional `degradation_class` and `evidence_kind` with those closed lists, and every existing finding fixture still validates unchanged. [verify: exec `bun test src/contracts/ src/review/`]
+- AC4: `keryx review ingest` downgrades a `review-degradation` finding of `major` or `blocker` that has no `evidence_kind` to `info`, records it in `scope.md` under its own heading with the rule name, and prints it on the terminal; a finding with evidence keeps its severity; findings of other reviewers are not touched. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/degradation-screen.test.ts`]
+- AC5: The reviewer payload carries the `keryx gdgraph affected` consumers of each changed shared export, with a recorded cap, and the summary states whether the cap dropped consumers. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/degradation-payload.test.ts`]
+- AC6: The reviewer is in profile `full` and not in `recommended`; a `delta` round (FIX slice) dispatches it only when the slice touches a shared symbol. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/coverage.test.ts src/review/dispatch.test.ts src/review/slice-routing.test.ts`]
+- AC7: Its findings appear in the TUI review panel and reviews inspector with class and evidence kind, and findings downgraded for missing evidence are marked as unproven. [verify: exec `bun test src/tui/review-panel.test.ts src/tui/reviews-inspector.test.ts`]
+- AC8: `review-orchestrator` (both copies, byte-identical, under its line ceiling) lists the reviewer, its profile and when it is dispatched. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/`]
+- AC9: README, the docs-site review guide and CHANGELOG describe the reviewer, the classes, the evidence rule and the downgrade. [verify: exec `bun run docs:check`]
+- AC10: A replay on 3 to 5 of the operator's own pull requests in the private frontend project, read-only, with the human lead reviewer's regression and quality findings as hand-labelled ground truth (kept in the session scratchpad, never committed), reports per PR how many ground-truth findings were reproduced at the same or an adjacent severity and how many `major` or above findings were judged wrong by a human. Draft thresholds, confirmed by the operator: at least half reproduced and at most one unconfirmed `major` per PR. The public report is anonymous: counts and classes only. [verify: judged]
+- AC11: The skill, bundle and docs contain no reference to a private project's pipeline, rule names or paths, and this flow wires the reviewer into no project's own pipeline. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/review-degradation-skill.test.ts`]
+- AC12: After the trial a report states the cost of a round with the reviewer against the same round without it (tokens, wall time, findings kept after ingest) and its effectiveness (AC10 numbers); whether it moves from `full` to `recommended` or the core set is recorded as the operator's decision, not written by the agent. [verify: judged]

+1. [1.962] Findings reach a review round through the report's keryx:findings block, and a round without one silently records none (known-mistake/accepted) - known-mistakes/review-ingest-discards-verdicts.md
+   `keryx review ingest --report <md>` reads structured findings from a fenced ` ```json keryx:findings ` block inside the report. A report without that block ingests as `findings: in=0`, and every `--verifications` claim naming one of its findings is then discarded as unresolvable — because the finding it names is not in the round.
+   claimType: known-mistake | confidence: high | version: 0.3.0
+   scope: module:review, flow, entity:parseEmbeddedFindings, ManagedReviewInput.findings, flow-complete gate
+   provenance: source=manual link=https://github.com/MrCipherSmith/keryx/pull/499 author=MrCipherSmith confirmedBy=flow 243 closed through the gate on round r06 with 3 findings, 3 refuted verdicts, 0 discarded
+   caveat: Version 0.2.0 of this entry asserted the opposite — that `review ingest`
+2. [1.913] A shell allowlist matched against the raw command string is not a security boundary (lesson/accepted) - lessons/allowlist-not-a-boundary.md
+   A remembered glob pattern that is matched against a command string which is then handed to `/bin/sh -c` grants far more than it appears to. The pattern matches text; the shell re-interprets that text. Verified, not theorised: a live allowlist contained `bash *`, `python3 *`, `curl *`, `cd *`, `# *`, `docker *`, `sudo *`, and the exact string `rm -rf /` — each an arbitrary-execution grant that auto-approved with no prompt.
+   claimType: lesson | confidence: high | version: 1.0.0
+   scope: module:src/lib, src/commands, src/tui, entity:shell-permissions, command-risk, approval gate
+   provenance: source=flow 115 (shell approval hardening), stress reports in `.metaproject/data/stress/` link=docs/decisions/keryx-harness/ADR-0009-destructive-command-escalation.md author=unknown confirmedBy=unknown

+   On PR #215 (flow 127, project registry) three consecutive review-fix rounds each introduced a new blocker while closing the previous one. The defect was not in any single fix; it was in treating a fix as finished once it addressed the reported symptom.
+   claimType: lesson | confidence: high | version: 0.5.0
+   scope: module:core, entity:project-registry
+   provenance: source=review rounds on PR #215 (flow 127), PR #216 (flow 128), PR #220 (flow 133) link=https://github.com/MrCipherSmith/keryx/pull/215 author=unknown confirmedBy=unknown
+4. [1.823] The keryx on PATH is a stale build; the review pipeline does not exercise the code under review (constraint/accepted) - constraints/stale-installed-keryx-binary.md
+   `~/.local/bin/keryx` is an installed build, and its version lags the working tree. It is NOT the working tree. Every `keryx …` invocation — including `keryx review ingest`, which is how a managed review package is recorded — runs that build, so the review pipeline routinely does not exercise the code being reviewed.
+   claimType: constraint | confidence: high | version: 0.1.0

+   A per-flag string allowlist that doesn't expand POSIX-bundled short flags rejects the idiomatic form of a tool's own CLI habits (`-il` vs `-i -l`); expand-then-check, not check-then-reject, for any allowlisted boolean-flag set.

+# review-degradation: a reviewer that checks whether the code got worse than on the base branch
+
+Status: frozen with the PRD `docs/requirements/keryx-review-degradation/prd.md` (operator, 2026-10-28).
+Source: user description (origin: human-request)
+
+## Problem
+
+`review-regression` checks only the dependents of a change through the code graph and its ingest screen refuses everything below `major`. Human lead reviewers of a large frontend project mostly ask a different question of the diff itself and of every consumer of a shared symbol it touched: is the code worse than on the base branch? Seven classes recur: behaviour delta, silent default change, diff versus description, debt introduced, performance delta, cross-PR hazard, and a test that cannot see the regression. Each was filed with evidence; findings without evidence were questions.
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+A generic keryx reviewer skill `review-degradation`, shipped in the npm package in profile `full`, whose findings carry a class and evidence, with the evidence rule enforced in code at ingest. After a trial on the operator's own PRs, its cost and effectiveness are measured and the operator decides on promotion.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- Запрос (дословно): «мне нужно, чтобы ты понял, нашел или предложил работать дополнительный скилл-ревьюер, который бы чекал именно подобные проблемы с регрессией, с ухудшением кода.» (source: helyx chat -1003908750902, voice message 230791, 2026-10-28)
+- Эффект (формализация агента): a review round in profile `full` also asks "is the code worse than on base" and returns classified, evidenced findings; major and above without evidence arrive as `info` and are listed as unproven.
+- Как наблюдать (предложение агента): `keryx review` on a diff with a behaviour change shows a `review-degradation` finding with class and evidence kind in the TUI review panel and in `scope.md`; the trial report gives reproduced-versus-ground-truth counts and the round cost.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Any change to `review-regression`, its screen or scope B dispatch.
+- Any change to the severity ladder or the exit criterion in `review-orchestrator`.
+- Wiring the reviewer into any private project's own review pipeline.
+- Style, naming and architecture of code the change did not touch.

+# Review: Degradation
+
+How this differs from `review-regression`, before anything else:
+
+| | `review-regression` | `review-degradation` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Looks at | dependents of the change only | the diff itself plus every consumer of each changed shared symbol |
+| Floor | `major`; below it the ingest screen refuses the finding | none: `blocker`, `major`, `minor`, `info` |
+| Set | the blast-radius files, refused in code if outside them | the consumers `keryx gdgraph affected` lists, never chosen by you |
+| Question | does the change break something that worked | is the code worse than on the base, and can you show it |
+
+`review-regression` is untouched by this reviewer and keeps its own screen. Do not re-file its findings; do not widen yours into its question.
+
+Your inputs are the reviewer payload only; session memory and earlier conversation are not inputs. You run no command unless your payload's `allowed_tools` says `run-tests`, except the read-only `git log`, `git blame` and `git show` where your host gives a read-only child git (keryx shell does not: there the payload supplies the history).
+
+## The one question
+
+> After this change, is the code worse than on the base branch: in behaviour, in defaults, in speed or in structure, and can that be shown?
+
+"Worse" is measured against the base branch, not against an ideal. Code that was
+already imperfect on the base is not a finding; it goes in the **pre-existing** lane.
+
+## Classes
+
+Every finding carries exactly one `degradation_class`:
+
+| Class | The change made the code worse by | Example shape |
+|---|---|---|
+| `behaviour-delta` | behaving differently from base on an input or event | an Escape key press handled by a nested popup now closes the parent |
+| `default-change` | moving a default or a normalisation | an empty value now falls to a different placeholder in every consumer of a shared component |
+| `diff-vs-description` | the description and the diff disagreeing | the description says shared code is unchanged, the diff edits it |
+| `debt` | adding structure that must be paid back | a second data model beside the existing one, a dead branch, a leftover of the old surface |
+| `performance` | making a path slower | every keystroke rebuilds all rows |
+| `cross-pr` | conflicting with another open change | whichever lands second silently drops the other's fix |
+| `blind-test` | a test that cannot see the regression | it uses the one input that works, or pins a neighbour of the changed symbol |
+
+## Evidence
+
+A finding is a claim; evidence is what makes it one. Every finding carries one
+`evidence_kind`, and `evidence` says what you ran or read:
+
+| Kind | What it is |
+|---|---|
+| `probe` | you ran the code, or a script against it, on head and on base, and the outputs differ |
+| `consumer-trace` | you followed a consumer of the changed symbol to its effect, file by file |
+| `merge-trace` | you merged two heads (or traced the merge) and showed what the second drops |
+| `red-test` | you wrote or named a test that fails on the head and passes on the base |
+| `base-diff` | you read the same path on base and on head and quote both |
+
+This is enforced, not requested. `keryx review ingest` lowers a `major` or
+`blocker` of this reviewer that has no `evidence_kind` to `info`, marks it unproven
+and lists it in `scope.md` under `## Degradation evidence screen` with the rule
+`degradation-no-evidence`. It is not rejected: a true claim survives, labelled. A
+finding with evidence keeps its severity; findings of other reviewers are not touched.
+Without a way to show it, file `info`, or a question.
+
+## What you are given
+
+- the diff, and the PR description when there is one;
+- the consumers of each changed shared export, from the code graph, with the cap
+  and what it dropped. The set is the graph's, not yours: trace those. If the cap
+  dropped consumers, say so in your summary; do not imply a complete sweep;
+- the flow's frozen acceptance criteria, and the previous round's findings.
+
+A change to a file the graph has no node for (a skill, a schema, a config) has no
+computed consumers. That is recorded as unresolved, not as clean; say the set could
+not answer the question.
+
+## How to look
+
+1. Read the diff against the description. Anything the description calls unchanged
+   and the diff edits is a `diff-vs-description` candidate.
+2. For each changed shared symbol, read its consumers before the symbol: the
+   assumption sits at the consumer, and the change moves what the consumer receives.
+3. Compare behaviour, not text. An event, a default, a fallback, an ordering, a
+   number of times a step runs: show it on head and on base.
+4. Count work per trigger: what runs on each keystroke, render, request.
+5. For each test the change added or leaned on, ask whether it would fail if the
+   regression were real.
+
+## Output lanes
+
+Four lanes, no more:
+
+- **Findings**: worse than base, with a class, evidence and `class_scope`.
+- **Questions**: `info` with `publication: "question"` when you suspect and cannot
+  show. A question is not a weak finding; it is a different thing to the reader.
+- **Pre-existing**: `location_class: "pre-existing"`. True, not caused by this change, not blocking.
+- **Verified clean**: in `summary`, one line per thing traced, and each line names
+  what was traced (the symbol, the consumers, the command). Silence must not read as "nothing found".
+
+## Class scope: required for `blocker` and `major`
+
+`class_scope` lists **every** site with the shape, and how you enumerated them. For
+this reviewer the sites are usually consumers; the enumeration is the walk over the
+graph's consumer list. "I checked the others" is not a method.
+
+```yaml
+class_scope:
+  sites: ["src/screens/a.ts:40", "src/screens/b.ts:12"]
+  enumeration_method: "every consumer of the changed component in the payload; 2 of 9 pass no value"
+```
+
+```markdown
+### [F-NNN] Title
+
+- **Severity**: blocker | major | minor | info
+- **Class**: behaviour-delta | default-change | diff-vs-description | debt | performance | cross-pr | blind-test
+- **Evidence kind**: probe | consumer-trace | merge-trace | red-test | base-diff
+- **File**: path/to/file.ts:line
+- **Problem**: what is worse than on base
+- **Why it matters**: impact
+- **Fix**: concrete suggestion

+### Shared laws (every reviewer)
+
+1. **A claim of runtime harm with no reproducible path is `info`.** If you cannot name the input, call, or condition that reaches the code, you have an observation, not a finding. Report it as `info` and say what would settle it.

+| "It looks worse, so it is a `major`." | Without an `evidence_kind` the ingest lowers it to `info` and marks it unproven. Show it, or file it as a question. |

 `review scope` bounds **the change**, and a review of it answers *is this change
 correct?* It does not answer *did this change break something that was working*.
 That is a second scope, and it is computed rather than browsed: `gdgraph
 affected` walked outward from every changed file, ranked by edge distance, cut at
 a depth and a file cap, closest first.
 
 | Flag | Description |
 |---|---|
 | `--ref <base>` | Take the changed-file list from `git diff --name-only` against this base. |
 | `--changed a,b` | Use this changed-file list instead of asking git. |
 | `--depth <n>` | Edge distance kept. Default **2**. |
 | `--max-files <n>` | File cap, closest first. Default **40**. |
 | `--no-related-tests` | Skip the naming-related tests of the changed files. |
 | `--package <review-dir>` | Read the graph built for that review at its PR head (refreshed first when the package has none), not the working tree's. |
 | `--previous <file>` | The previous round's `--json` record; decides whether this round must recompute. |
 | `--final` | This is the final round, so recompute regardless of what the changed-file set did. |

+# Review: Degradation
+
+How this differs from `review-regression`, before anything else:
+
+| | `review-regression` | `review-degradation` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Looks at | dependents of the change only | the diff itself plus every consumer of each changed shared symbol |
+| Floor | `major`; below it the ingest screen refuses the finding | none: `blocker`, `major`, `minor`, `info` |
+| Set | the blast-radius files, refused in code if outside them | the consumers `keryx gdgraph affected` lists, never chosen by you |
+| Question | does the change break something that worked | is the code worse than on the base, and can you show it |
+
+`review-regression` is untouched by this reviewer and keeps its own screen. Do not re-file its findings; do not widen yours into its question.
+
+Your inputs are the reviewer payload only; session memory and earlier conversation are not inputs. You run no command unless your payload's `allowed_tools` says `run-tests`, except the read-only `git log`, `git blame` and `git show` where your host gives a read-only child git (keryx shell does not: there the payload supplies the history).

+## The one question
+
+> After this change, is the code worse than on the base branch: in behaviour, in defaults, in speed or in structure, and can that be shown?
+
+"Worse" is measured against the base branch, not against an ideal. Code that was
+already imperfect on the base is not a finding; it goes in the **pre-existing** lane.
+
+## Classes
+
+Every finding carries exactly one `degradation_class`:
+
+| Class | The change made the code worse by | Example shape |
+|---|---|---|
+| `behaviour-delta` | behaving differently from base on an input or event | an Escape key press handled by a nested popup now closes the parent |
+| `default-change` | moving a default or a normalisation | an empty value now falls to a different placeholder in every consumer of a shared component |
+| `diff-vs-description` | the description and the diff disagreeing | the description says shared code is unchanged, the diff edits it |
+| `debt` | adding structure that must be paid back | a second data model beside the existing one, a dead branch, a leftover of the old surface |
+| `performance` | making a path slower | every keystroke rebuilds all rows |
+| `cross-pr` | conflicting with another open change | whichever lands second silently drops the other's fix |
+| `blind-test` | a test that cannot see the regression | it uses the one input that works, or pins a neighbour of the changed symbol |
+
+## Evidence
+
+A finding is a claim; evidence is what makes it one. Every finding carries one
+`evidence_kind`, and `evidence` says what you ran or read:
+
+| Kind | What it is |
+|---|---|
+| `probe` | you ran the code, or a script against it, on head and on base, and the outputs differ |
+| `consumer-trace` | you followed a consumer of the changed symbol to its effect, file by file |
+| `merge-trace` | you merged two heads (or traced the merge) and showed what the second drops |
+| `red-test` | you wrote or named a test that fails on the head and passes on the base |
+| `base-diff` | you read the same path on base and on head and quote both |

+`blocker` of this reviewer that has no `evidence_kind` to `info`, marks it unproven

+finding with evidence keeps its severity; findings of other reviewers are not touched.
+Without a way to show it, file `info`, or a question.

+
+- the diff, and the PR description when there is one;
+- the consumers of each changed shared export, from the code graph, with the cap
+  and what it dropped. The set is the graph's, not yours: trace those. If the cap

+## How to look

+1. Read the diff against the description. Anything the description calls unchanged

+2. For each changed shared symbol, read its consumers before the symbol: the

+4. Count work per trigger: what runs on each keystroke, render, request.
+5. For each test the change added or leaned on, ask whether it would fail if the

+Your payload may carry a `layers` block for your files: the files the graph says are affected, symbol neighbours, related tests, the wiki pages that describe the files and the memory entries for their module. It is bounded, and `truncated` names what was cut and the command that fetches the rest. When the diff alone does not settle a question, ask the project. Each command below is read-only and calls no model.

+- `keryx gdgraph affected <file>`: who depends on the file. Use it before you call a change contained, and whenever a changed export, signature or behaviour may have callers outside your files.
+- `keryx test related <file>`: the tests that cover the file. Use it before you say a behaviour is untested, and to judge whether a test would fail if the code broke.
+- `keryx wiki ask "<q>"`: what the project wiki says a module is for and which rules bind it. Use it when the intent of the code is unclear and the diff does not state it.
+- `keryx memory search "<q>"`: recorded lessons, decisions and known mistakes. Use it before you report a pattern the project may already have decided on, and when a failure looks like one it has seen.
